threads.thread_goal: Align on current cleaning and changeover practices and main issues.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Cross-Line Hygiene and Changeover Optimization work.
For the food side, can everyone share how you currently run cleaning and changeover on your line? Rough steps and how long each part usually takes is enough for now.
We will use this to complete task T1 and feed into the time tracking sheet A4 for the pilot.
Please call out where you see delays or confusion during cleaning or changeover.

On my food line we usually do:
- Stop line and lock out
- Quick dry scrape of product
- Rinse with warm water
- Foam wash
- Rinse again
- Visual check and start up
Whole thing is around 45 to 60 minutes if nothing goes wrong.
Biggest delay is waiting for someone with a forklift to move pallets out of the way so we can reach the back guards.

My routine is similar but we add a short pre-rinse before scraping because otherwise the product sticks too much.
Steps:
- Pre-rinse
- Scrape
- Main rinse
- Foam
- Final rinse
- Quick swab by QA when they are available
Time is closer to 70 minutes when we wait for QA.
Pain point is that we do not always know when QA will come, so we sometimes sit idle with the line ready.

Adding my view from the night shift.
We follow the same basic steps but changeover adds:
- Empty hoppers and weigh remaining material
- Swap over tooling and guards
- Adjust settings on the control panel
Cleaning itself is about 40 minutes, but changeover including setup is more like 90 minutes.
Main issues:
- Tools not always where they should be
- No clear place to log when we find residue after restart
This will be important for T1 and later when we fill A4 with real times.

On my side I just follow the posted sheet on the wall.
I think it is:
- Stop
- Rinse
- Soap
- Rinse
- Check
I am not sure about the exact minutes for each step, I just know the supervisor wants us under 60 minutes total.
I can start timing each part next shift if that helps for A4, but I might need someone to show me how you want it written.

From the metal sawing area side, for T2 our current cleaning and chip-removal routine is:
- Stop saw and isolate energy
- Use scraper and brush to remove chips from table and guides
- Blow compressed air around the blade housing
- Wipe oil splashes from guards and floor area
- Check chip bin and empty if close to full
This takes about 25 to 35 minutes per machine.
Pain points:
- Chips accumulate under the conveyor where we do not have easy access
- When forklifts pass through, they sometimes drag chips toward the food corridor
We should capture these details clearly in T2 so we can later align with the food side.

Thanks for laying that out.
For T2, can you also note which tools you use for each step and where chips tend to build up the most? That will help when we compare with the food line cleaning and think about shared forklift routes.
We will also need to log the time per step in A4 once we pick the pilot machine.

Yes, I can break it down.
Tools:
- Long-handled scraper for table and guides
- Stiff brush for corners
- Air gun for blade housing
- Floor squeegee for oil spots
Frequent chip buildup:
- Under the infeed conveyor
- Around the blade guard lower edge
- In the floor expansion joints near the shared walkway
I will document this in the T2 notes and estimate minutes per step so we can plug into A4 later.

For the food lines, we should also capture where we depend on other teams.
Examples from my line:
- Waiting for maintenance to unlock a guard that sticks
- Waiting for QA to release after cleaning
- Waiting for forklift to clear pallets
If we list these in T1 with rough wait times, A4 will show where the real downtime is, not just the washing itself.

I can sit with you next shift and help time each step.
We can write down:
- Start and end time for each cleaning step
- Any waiting time in between
Then we can pass that to whoever is maintaining A4.
This will also complete part of T1 for our line.

To move forward we need to pick one food line and one metal saw as pilots.
Proposal:
- Food pilot line: the cereal packing line where most of us rotate
- Metal pilot machine: the main saw closest to the shared corridor
These seem to have the most interaction with forklifts and shared walkways, so they are good test cases.
If no one objects by tomorrow, we will log this as our pilot choice for D1 and start filling A4 for those two first.

From the metal side I am fine using the main saw by the corridor as the pilot.
It is the one that creates the most chips near shared traffic, so if we can keep that one under control the others will be easier.
I will start tracking step times on that machine for A4 and complete T2 details there first.

Agree on using the cereal packing line as the food pilot.
It has frequent changeovers and we already know the main pain points.
For A4, I suggest we capture at least:
- Start and end time for full cleaning and changeover
- Time per main step
- Waiting time by reason, like QA, forklift, maintenance
- Any re-cleaning needed after restart
If everyone is ok with that, we can treat this as the base structure for D2.

The list for A4 makes sense to me.
Maybe we also add who was on the shift, just initials, so if we see a big difference we can ask how they did it.
I can start writing down times and reasons for waits on the cereal line next shift to help close T1.

For the metal saw, I will mirror the same structure in A4:
- Total cleaning time
- Time per step
- Waiting time, for example if we wait for chip bin to be emptied by forklift
- Any rework if we find chips after restart
That way T2 and T1 data are comparable.
I support using this as the agreed content for D2.

Summarizing for closure:
- D1: Pilot assets will be the cereal packing food line and the main metal saw by the shared corridor.
- D2: A4 will capture total time, time per step, waiting time with reason, re-cleaning events, and operator initials for both areas.
Next step is to complete T1 and T2 mapping for those assets first, then extend to the other lines.

threads.thread_goal: Draft and refine the new cleaning and changeover checklists.

messages.text:
Sharing first drafts of the new cleaning checklists so we can refine them.
For the food line CIP checklist A1 linked to T3, I structured it as:
1. Pre-rinse and product removal
2. Wash with foam and brushes
3. Rinse and drain
4. Visual verification and restart checks
For the metal side, A2 from T6 is roughly:
1. Chip removal
2. Oil and dust wipe-down
3. Visual verification around blade and guards
Please review the sequence and call out anything missing or out of order before we lock them in.

On the food checklist A1, I think we should split pre-rinse into two steps:
- Quick pre-rinse to soften product
- Main rinse after scraping
Right now I usually do that anyway, and it affects time tracking.
Also, where do we note lockout and chemical safety? I did not see that in the short version.

Good catch.
For A1 under T3 we should probably structure it as:
0. Prepare area and lockout
1. Pre-rinse
2. Scrape and remove product
3. Main rinse
4. Foam wash and contact time
5. Final rinse and drain
6. Visual verification and restart checks
I will add safety lockout and chemical handling notes into step 0 and 4 so it is clear.

For the food side, can we also include a quick check that tools and guards are back in place before restart?
Sometimes after cleaning we forget a small cover or a wrench on the frame.
Maybe in A1 under visual verification we list:
- All guards closed
- No tools left inside
- No visible residue or foam
That would help with T3 definition of done.

I like that A1 is short, but I am not sure where to tick off each step.
Will it be one line per step with a box, or just a free text area?
For me it is easier if it is just:
- Step name
- Box to tick
- Space for initials
So I do not have to write much during cleaning.

The idea for A1 is exactly that: one line per step with a tick box and initials.
We will keep it to one page so it can stay near the line.
For T3 we also need to make sure at least two operators from different shifts review it, so thanks for the feedback.
I will update the draft with the extra pre-rinse and the guard and tool checks.

On the metal checklist A2 for T6, I suggest we be more explicit around the blade and guards.
Proposed sequence:
1. Isolate energy and lockout
2. Remove chips from table and guides
3. Clean around blade housing and lower guard
4. Sweep and wipe floor area, including under conveyor if reachable
5. Check chip bin and empty if needed
6. Visual verification of chips, oil, and dust in critical zones
This will make it easier to highlight the safety zones we need to check every time.

Looks solid.
For T6 we also need maintenance to validate the critical zones.
I will ask them to review A2 and confirm if we missed any area around the blade or guards.
Once they sign off, we can treat that as the standard sequence.

One more thought on A1.
During wash we sometimes need to soak stubborn spots longer.
Should we add a note like minimum contact time for foam so people do not rush it?
Maybe just a reminder under the foam step instead of a separate step, so the checklist stays short.

Agree, we can add a short note under the foam step in A1: keep foam on surfaces for the required contact time before rinsing.
No need for a separate line.
That keeps T3 aligned with safety guidance without making the checklist too long.

For A2 visual checks, I propose we list the critical zones explicitly to close T6:
- Around blade and lower guard
- Under infeed conveyor
- Floor area in front of operator station
- Floor expansion joints near shared walkway
Operators can scan these four spots before removing lockout.

To close this out we need to confirm the structure and sequence for both checklists.
For A1 under T3, the final structure is:
0. Prepare area and lockout, including chemical safety
1. Pre-rinse
2. Scrape and remove product
3. Main rinse
4. Foam wash with contact time
5. Final rinse and drain
6. Visual verification including guards, tools, and residue
For A2 under T6, the final structure is:
1. Isolate energy and lockout
2. Remove chips from table and guides
3. Clean around blade housing and lower guard
4. Sweep and wipe floor area, including under conveyor where possible
5. Check and empty chip bin if needed
6. Visual verification of chips, oil, and dust in the four critical zones listed above
If there are no objections, we will treat this as approval for D3 and D4.

No objections from my side.
The sequences for A1 and A2 look clear and match how we actually work, with the safety and visual checks spelled out.
We can move ahead and print test versions for the pilot lines once we start T7 and T8.

threads.thread_goal: Define rules for shared equipment and forklift hygiene between areas.

messages.text:
We need to align on hygiene rules for forklifts and shared tools moving between food and metal zones.
Right now there is no clear routine, and we have seen chips and dust near the food corridor.
We have a draft for the shared equipment checklist A3 under T4, but it needs input from both sides.
Let us define the minimum cleaning steps before a forklift enters food areas and how often we log these checks.

From the metal side, the main risk is chips stuck on forklift wheels and forks.
For A3 I suggest minimum steps before entering food areas:
- Visual check of wheels and forks
- Brush off any visible chips from wheels, forks, and mast base
- Quick wipe of forks if there is oil
This can be done in under 3 minutes if we keep a brush and rag at the crossing point.

On the food side, I would add a quick floor check where the forklift stops.
Sometimes chips fall when it brakes.
Maybe A3 can include:
- Check floor around stop point and sweep if needed
Also, for shared tools like brooms or shovels, we should not move them from metal to food without cleaning them first.

I am a bit unsure where we will keep the brush and rag for the forklift.
If it is too far, people will skip it.
Could we add in A3 that cleaning tools must be stored at the gate between metal and food, so it is obvious and quick?

For logging, I am worried that if we have to write too much, it will not happen.
Maybe A3 can just have:
- Time
- Forklift ID
- Tick box that wheels, forks, and floor were checked
And we only log when entering the food area, not every move inside metal.

Agree, we should keep logging light.
For D6 we can say: log once per forklift per entry into the food zone, not every trip inside.
A3 can be a small sheet near the gate with one line per entry.
That should keep it under 5 minutes as required in T4.

On shared tools, I suggest we mark some tools as food-only and some as metal-only.
For tools that must be shared, A3 can require:
- Brush or wipe tool to remove chips or food residue
- Visual check before crossing the line between areas
We can also color-code handles so it is clear which tools stay where.

Putting this together for A3 under T4, the minimum steps before a forklift enters food areas could be:
1. Visual check of wheels and forks
2. Brush off visible chips from wheels, forks, and mast base
3. Wipe forks if there is oil
4. Check floor around stop point and sweep if needed
5. Log entry on the small sheet with time, forklift ID, and tick box
Does everyone agree this is the right minimum for D5?

Works for me.
If we keep the brush and broom right at the gate like mentioned, it should not slow us down much.
I support using that list as the minimum steps for D5.

Agreed from metal side as well.
The sequence is practical and fits into the 3 to 5 minute window.
We just need to make sure the gate area has enough space to sweep safely.
I also support logging once per entry as defined for D6.

To summarize and close:
- D5: Before a forklift enters food areas, operators must follow the five-step check in A3: visual check, brush wheels and forks, wipe oily forks, sweep floor at stop point, and log the entry.
- D6: Hygiene checks for forklifts are logged once per forklift per entry into the food zone on a simple sheet near the gate.
T4 will now be updated so A3 reflects these rules and stays under 5 minutes to complete.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and review pilot runs for new procedures on selected lines.

messages.text:
We are ready to start pilot runs for the new cleaning and changeover routines.
As agreed earlier, pilots will be on the cereal packing food line and the main metal saw by the shared corridor.
We need to confirm the pilot schedule, which shifts go first, and how we will record times in A4 while running T7 and T8.
Please share any constraints from your shifts before we lock the plan.

For the food line, I suggest we start the pilot on the afternoon shift.
Morning is usually packed with urgent orders, and we have less room for testing.
Afternoon can run at least three full changeovers over two days without risking a long stop.
I can take care of filling A4 for those runs under T7.

I am on the morning shift most days.
If we start with afternoon like suggested, I can join on day two to see how it works and then repeat the same steps on morning shift later.
For A4, do we need one sheet per changeover or can we log multiple runs on the same sheet?

For the pilot under T7 and T8, let us use one line per changeover or cleaning cycle on A4.
So one sheet can hold several runs, but each run has its own row with start and end times and notes.
That will make it easier to compare the three pilot runs.

On the metal saw, the quietest window is usually late evening.
I propose we run the three pilot cleaning cycles for T8 on the late shift over three consecutive days.
That way we can follow the full A2 checklist without pressure from urgent cuts.
I will handle A4 entries for the saw during those runs.

For the food line, I just want to confirm we will not stop production for more than 2 hours.
If we follow A1 and the new steps, do we expect cleaning plus changeover to stay under that?
I am ok to support on afternoon shift as long as we have that limit clear.

Based on our current times, we should be under 90 minutes even with the extra checks in A1.
We will monitor closely on A4 during the first run.
If we see it going over, we will pause and adjust the sequence before the next run so we stay within the 2 hour limit.

I can help with timing on the second and third pilot runs on the food line.
Sometimes I forget to note exact minutes, so if someone can show me the first time on A4, I will copy the same way.
Just let me know which days we are doing it.

One more point for the metal pilot.
During T8 runs we should also note any extra sweeping needed around the shared walkway, since that is where chips can travel toward food.
I will add a small comment field on A4 for that.

Let us lock the pilot schedule so everyone can plan.
Proposal for D7:
- Food line T7: three pilot changeovers on the afternoon shift over the next two days, with A4 filled by 433963 and support from 102838 and 558848.
- Metal saw T8: three pilot cleaning cycles on the late shift over the next three days, with A4 filled by 310108.
If there are no conflicts, we will confirm this as the plan.

No conflict from my side.
I confirm I can cover the three afternoon pilot runs on the food line and handle A4 entries for T7.
We will also note any issues with the new A1 checklist so we can tweak it later.

Confirmed for the metal saw as well.
I will run the three late-shift cleaning cycles and log times and notes in A4 for T8.
We will pay attention to chip spread near the shared walkway and record any extra cleaning needed.

Great, summarizing D7:
- Food pilot T7: afternoon shift, three changeovers over two days on the cereal packing line, with A4 filled each run.
- Metal pilot T8: late shift, three cleaning cycles over three days on the main corridor saw, with A4 filled each run.
After the pilots we will compare times to the baseline and adjust before full rollout.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize procedures, training briefing, and incident logging routine.

messages.text:
We have completed the pilot runs on the cereal packing line and the main metal saw.
Time tracking in A4 shows that cleaning and changeover stayed within the 2 hour limit and we reduced re-cleaning events.
I have drafted the final procedure summary A7, the operator briefing A5 for T9, and a simple incident log A6 for T10.
Let us review these and agree on the go-live date for all shifts.

Quick summary of pilot results from A4 for everyone:
- Food line: average cleaning plus changeover time was 82 minutes, with fewer delays waiting for QA thanks to clearer sequence in A1.
- Metal saw: average cleaning time was 32 minutes, with better chip control around the shared walkway using A2 and A3.
No incidents were logged during the pilots.
Based on this, A7 now reflects the final standard steps for both areas.

On the metal side, A7 looks consistent with what we tested.
The only suggestion I have is to highlight that the chip check near the shared walkway is mandatory after every cleaning, not optional.
For the briefing A5, it would help to include one example photo of good and bad cleaning around the blade guard.

For the food line, A7 and A5 match what we did in the pilot.
The toolbox talk format in A5 is clear.
I like that it calls out common mistakes like skipping the foam contact time or forgetting tools inside.
For A6, I just want to confirm what we must write when we see an issue.

On A6 the incident log, the fields are:
- Date and shift
- Area (food line or metal saw)
- Short description of issue
- Quick fix applied
- Initials
It is meant to be filled in less than 2 minutes during or right after the shift.
Supervisors will review A6 weekly and capture key points in A8 for shift handover.

On the training side, how will we run A5 across all shifts?
Will it be one big session or short talks at shift start?
I think short 10 to 15 minute talks at the line would work better for us.

Plan for T9 is to use A5 as a 10 to 15 minute toolbox talk at the start of each shift for one week.
We will cover:
- Key changes in A1, A2, and A3
- Examples of common mistakes from the pilot
- How to use A6 and A8
Supervisors will lead the talks, and we will keep attendance lists so we know who still needs the briefing.

For A6, if I see a small residue after restart and we stop to clean it, should I log that too or only bigger issues?
I do not want to overfill the sheet, but I also do not want to miss something important.

Good question.
For A6 we should log:
- Any hygiene issue that causes a stop or re-cleaning
- Any repeated pattern, even if small, like the same spot needing extra cleaning every day
If it is a one-off tiny residue that you fix in seconds, no need to log.
This way T10 stays manageable and still useful.

For A8 shift handover notes, can we add a small section just for metal saw cleaning status?
Something like:
- Last full cleaning done at
- Any pending cleaning or chip hotspots
That will help the next shift know if they need to plan extra time.

Yes, we can add that to A8.
We will mirror it for the food line as well:
- Last full cleaning and changeover time
- Any pending hygiene checks or known trouble spots
That will close the loop between A4, A6, and A8.

We now need to agree on the final go-live date and confirm that A7 is our single reference for procedures.
Proposal for D8:
- Approve A7 as the final standard for food and metal cleaning and changeover.
- Start full rollout next Monday, with A5 toolbox talks running that week and A6 and A8 in use from day one.
Does anyone see a reason to delay?

No issues from my side.
Starting next Monday works, and A7 is clear enough to follow on the floor.
As long as we have printed copies near the lines, I am good with D8.

Agreed from metal side.
A7 captures the final A2 and A3 steps correctly, and next Monday gives us enough time to brief everyone.
I support D8 and will make sure the saw area has the new checklists posted.

Summarizing D8 and next steps:
- D8: A7 is approved as the final cross-area procedure summary, and go-live for all shifts is next Monday.
- A5 toolbox talks will run on each shift next week as part of T9.
- A6 incident log and A8 shift handover notes will be used from day one as part of T10 and T12.
We will print and post all checklists and summaries in the relevant areas before Friday.
